Rashi on Gittin 22a:10:1.hebrew: טבל וחולין מעורבין זה בזה - אין לך פירי באילן הזה שאין מקצתו מן הארץ שהוא טבל, ומקצתו מחוצה לארץ שהוא חולין, לפי שהיניקה מתערבת; ונפקא מינה שאין מעשרין מטבל ודאי עליו, דהוי מן החיוב על הפטור, ולא ממנו על טבל ודאי:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:10:1.english: Untithed produce and non-sacred produce are mixed together - There is no fruit on this tree that is not partly from the Land [of Israel], which is tevel [untithed produce], and partly from outside the Land, which is chullin [non-sacred, exempt produce], because the nourishment mixes together. And the practical difference is that one may not separate tithes from definite tevel for it, since that would be [separating] from the obligated for the exempt, nor from it for definite tevel:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:10:2.english: That which grows in [a place of] obligation - that which is within the Land of Israel:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:11:1.hebrew: מקצת נופו כו' - ואע"פ שכל שרשיו בארץ או בחו"ל, אלמא אזלינן בתר נוף:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:11:1.english: Some of its branches, etc. - And even though all of its roots are in the Land [of Israel] or outside the Land [of Israel], thus [we see that] we follow the branches:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:12:1.hebrew: מ"ט דרבן שמעון - מהו "הגדל בחיוב חייב"? והלא היניקה של שרשין מעלה שרף בכל הפרי, ושורשי עבר זה מעלים שרף לפרי שבעבר זה:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:12:1.english: What is the reasoning of Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel] - What is [the meaning of his statement], "that which grows in [the] obligated [area] is obligated"? Does not the absorption by the roots bring sap up into all the fruit, and the roots of this side bring sap up to the fruit on the other side:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:12:2.hebrew: דמפסיק צונמא - שן סלע מבדיל באמצע השרשים ומפסיקין עד הגזע, הלכך לרבן שמעון לא ינקי מהדדי:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:12:2.english: [Because] a rock divides [them] - A crag of rock separates in the middle of the roots, and [they] are separated up to the trunk; therefore, according to Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel], they do not draw nourishment from one another:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:13:1.english: As they then become mixed - For the tree from the trunk upward is whole [and undivided]:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:14:1.hebrew: מר סבר אוירא מבלבל - אע"פ שכל מה שיש מן השרשין בקרקע הוי מובדל, הואיל וכשיצא לאויר הוא מעורב ומבלבל וינקי מהדדי:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:14:1.english: One Sage holds [that] the air mixes [them] - Even though whatever of the roots is in the ground is separated, since when it emerges into the air it is mixed and intermingled and they draw [nourishment] from one another:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:14:2.hebrew: ומ"ס - אוירא לא מבלבל, הואיל ובתוך הקרקע מובדל בסלע שאינו מצמיח; ומיהו היכא דכל שרשיו בא"י, ליכא מאן דאזיל בתר נוף:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:14:2.english: And [the other] Sage holds - [That] the air does not mix [the nutrients], since within the ground [the tree] is separated by a rock that does not produce growth; however, where all of its roots are in the Land of Israel, there is no one who follows [the location of] the branches:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:15:1.english: There are three hides - [They] differ in their names and in their measurements:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:16:1.english: As per its plain meaning - Like this matzah, which was not prepared with leavening in the manner of [regular] bread:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:16:2.english: Treated with flour [kemiach] - processed with flour:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:16:3.english: For what halakha - [are] their measures different:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:16:4.hebrew: משקולת - של עופרת עשויה להיות פוחתת, ומחפין אותה בעור שלא תהא נשופת ופוחתת:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:16:4.english: A weight - [One] of lead is prone to diminishing, and they cover it with leather so that it will not be rubbed down and diminish:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:16:5.english: A quarter of a quarter - [It] was a small weight of theirs:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:17:1.hebrew: חיפה - מתוקן קצת, וראוי לחפות בו קמיעין:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:17:1.english: Ḥifa - [Hide that is] somewhat prepared, and fit to cover amulets with it:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:18:1.hebrew: לכתוב עליו את הגט - כרבנן דמכשרי. ומיהו קלף גמור דמליח וקמיח ואפיץ לא שמיה עור, משום הכי לא מני בהדייהו. ושיעוריה תנן בהמוציא יין (שבת דף עט:): "קלף כדי לכתוב בו פרשה קטנה שבתפילין", אבל דיפתרא אינו כשר לתפילין, הילכך שיעורו בגט:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:18:1.english: To write a bill of divorce on it - [This is] in accordance with the Rabbis, who rule [it] valid. However, complete parchment [klaf], which is salted, treated with flour, and treated with gallnuts, is not called "hide"; therefore, it was not counted among them. And its measure [for Shabbat] we learned in [the chapter] Hamotzi Yayin (Shabbat 79b): "Klaf — enough to write on it the smallest section in tefillin." But diftera is not valid for tefillin; therefore, its measure is [the amount needed] for a bill of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:19:1.hebrew: מאן חכמים - כלומר, מאן נינהו ומאי טעמייהו דמכשרי:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:19:1.english: Who are the Rabbis - That is to say, who are they, and what is their reason for deeming [them] valid:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:1:1.english: As he takes it - [meaning] the pot, and gives [it] to her:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:1:2.hebrew: שמא יקטום - העלה, והויא קציצה מן המחובר:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:1:2.english: Lest he detach - the leaf, and it is [a case of] cutting from what is attached:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:2:1.hebrew: עד שיחזיק בזרעים - עציץ הוי תלוש ומיקני במשיכה, זרעים הוי מחוברין ודינן כקרקע, ונקנים בכסף בשטר ובחזקה. ו"עד שיחזיק" — כגון דניכש או עידר, דהויא חזקה. ובלא יהיב מעות קמיירי, דאי יהיב זוזי — מיקנו בכסף:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:2:1.english: Until he takes possession of the plants - A pot is detached [from the ground] and is acquired by pulling; [whereas] plants are [considered] attached [to the ground], and their law is like [that of] land, and they are acquired by money, by a document, or by an act of taking possession. And "until he takes possession" [means] for example that he weeded or hoed, which is an act of taking possession. And [the Gemara] is speaking of [a case] where he did not give money, for if he had given money, they would be acquired by money:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:4:1.hebrew: החזיק בעציץ - ולא משכו לקנות, אלא עשה בו שום מלאכה במקומו:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:4:1.english: [If] he took possession of the pot - and he did not pull it to acquire [it], rather he performed some work on it in its place:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:4:2.english: He does not even acquire the pot - because movable property is not acquired through taking possession:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:5:1.hebrew: נקבו בארץ ונופו בחוצה לארץ - שהיה מונח על הגבול, ונוף הזרעים נוטה חוץ לעציץ, חוץ לגבול:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:5:1.english: Its perforation is in the Land [of Israel] and its foliage is outside the Land - That [the pot] was placed on the border, and the foliage of the plants extends outside the pot, outside the border:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:5:2.english: We follow its perforation - Because it draws nourishment from there, and [therefore] it is obligated in tithes:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:5:3.english: We follow its branches - and it is exempt from tithes by Torah law [as produce] outside the Land [of Israel]:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:6:1.english: Where it took root - [extending] outside the perforation, within the ground of the Land of Israel:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:6:2.hebrew: כולי עלמא לא פליגי - דלא אזלי' תו בתר נוף, הואיל ומחובר ממש בארץ:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:6:2.english: No one disagrees - that we no longer follow the branches, since it is literally attached to the ground:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:7:1.english: And where it took root, do they not disagree? - [Is there] no one who follows the foliage?

Rashi on Gittin 22a:7:2.hebrew: שתי גנות זו על גב זו - וזו אצל זו, וקרקעית האחת גבוה מחברתה, וגידור שלה זקוף, והירק בינתים בגידור הגבוהה, דעכשיו הוא נשרש בקרקעו של עליון, ונופו באוירו של תחתון:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:7:2.english: Two gardens, one above the other - and [they are] one next to the other, and the ground of one is higher than [that of] its neighbor, and its embankment is vertical, and the vegetables are between them, in the embankment of the upper [garden], so that now it is rooted in the ground of the upper [owner] and its foliage is in the airspace of the lower [owner]:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:7:3.english: [It] belongs to the lower [owner] - we follow the foliage:

Rashi on Gittin 22a:8:1.hebrew: כדקתני טעמא - שאם ירצה תחתון למלאות גנתו כו', והואיל ובידו למחות וגורם לירק הזה, זוכה בה, ולאו משום הטיית נוף:
Rashi on Gittin 22a:8:1.english: As it teaches the reason - For if the lower [owner] wishes to fill his garden, etc., and since it is in his power to protest and he is the cause of this vegetable [growing], he acquires it, and [it is] not because of the leaning of the branches:

Tosafot on Gittin 22a:15:1.hebrew: לא על נייר מחוק - שהכתב על הנייר שאינו מחוק, ועדיו על המחק; אבל שניהם על המחק כשר, כדאמרי' בריש גט פשוט (ב"ב קסד.), דאינו דומה נמחק פעם אחת לנמחק שתי פעמים:
Tosafot on Gittin 22a:15:1.english: Not on erased paper - [This refers to a case] where the text is on paper that is not erased, and its witnesses [are signed] on the erasure; however, [if] both of them are on the erasure, it is valid, as we say at the beginning of [the chapter] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 164a), that [something] erased once is not comparable to [something] erased twice:

Tosafot on Gittin 22a:15:2.hebrew: שלש עורות הן - פי' בקונטרס דקלף גמור לא חשיב בהדייהו, דלא שמיה עור. ועוד אומר ר"י דלא מני בהדייהו קלף, משום דבהדיא תנן ששיעורו כדי לכתוב פרשה קטנה שבתפילין; ואף על גב דשיעור חיפה, דהוי כדי לעשות קמיע, שנוי במשנה, מ"מ לא הזכיר חיפה בהדיא במתני':
Tosafot on Gittin 22a:15:2.english: There are three hides - Rashi explained that [Ulla] does not count finished parchment among them, because it is not called "hide." And Rabbeinu Yitzchak further says that [Ulla] did not list parchment among them because we explicitly learned in the Mishnah that its [minimum] measure is enough to write a small passage of tefillin; and even though the measure of ḥifa—which is enough to make an amulet—is taught in the Mishnah, nevertheless, [the Mishnah] did not mention ḥifa explicitly in the Mishnah:

Tosafot on Gittin 22a:18:1.hebrew: כדי לכתוב עליו את הגט - היינו כרבנן דמכשרי אדיפתרא, ולהכי מייתי לה הכא. ואלו השיעורין אינן לפי חשיבות העור, דיש שהוא חשוב ושיעורו גדול מן הגרוע ממנו, אלא כל א' שיעורו במה שרגילין לעשות ממנו:
Tosafot on Gittin 22a:18:1.english: Enough to write a bill of divorce upon it - This is in accordance with the Rabbis who validate [a bill of divorce written] on diftera, and for this reason [the Gemara] cites it here. And these measures are not according to the value of the hide, for there is [a type] that is [more] valuable, yet its measure is larger than [that of] one inferior to it; rather, each one's measure is according to what people are accustomed to make from it:

Tosafot on Gittin 22a:19:1.hebrew: מאן חכמים ר' אלעזר - פי' בקונטרס: דאמר עדי מסירה עיקר, והבאה להנשא צריכה להביא עדי מסירה. ודוקא הכא, על דבר שיכול להזדייף, אומר רש"י דצריכה עדי מסירה בשעה שבאת להנשא; אבל בגיטין הכתובים בדבר שאינו יכול להזדייף, יכולה להנשא ע"י עדי חתימה, ואפילו לר' אלעזר, כדתנן בפ' בתרא (לקמן גיטין פו.) ומייתי ליה בריש מכילתין: שאין העדים חותמין על הגט אלא מפני תיקון העולם. אבל מה שפי' בקונטרס דלר' מאיר, אשה הבאה לינשא בגט הכתוב על דבר שיכול להזדייף אינה צריכה עדי מסירה, ועדים החתומים בו אינה מביאה לפנינו אם יש מכירין חתימתן, ואי הוה ביה תנאה וזייפתיה ליכא דידע — משמע דאי הוי סהדי קמן, הוה כשר; ואי אפשר לומר כן, דלר' מאיר בעינן שיהא מוכח מתוכו, כדמשמע בריש כל הגט (לקמן גיטין כד:), ובדבר שיכול להזדייף אין מוכיח מתוכו כלום:
Tosafot on Gittin 22a:19:1.english: Who are the Rabbis? Rabbi Elazar - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres: [It is Rabbi Elazar,] who says that the witnesses to the delivery are primary, and [a woman] who comes to remarry must bring witnesses to the delivery. And specifically here, [when the get is written] on something that can be forged, Rashi says that she needs witnesses to the delivery at the time she comes to remarry; but with bills of divorce written on something that cannot be forged, she may remarry on the basis of the signatory witnesses, even according to Rabbi Elazar — as we learned in the last chapter (below, Gittin 86a), and [the Gemara] cites it at the beginning of our tractate: "Witnesses sign on a get only for the betterment of the world." However, as for what [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres — that according to Rabbi Meir, a woman who comes to remarry with a get written on something that can be forged does not need witnesses to the delivery, and she does not bring the witnesses signed on it before us if there are [others] who recognize their signatures, and if there were a condition in it and she forged it [out], there would be no one who knows — this implies that if the [signatory] witnesses were before us, it would be valid! But it is impossible to say so, because according to Rabbi Meir we require that [the get] be self-evident from within itself, as is implied at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Kol HaGet (below, Gittin 24b), and with something that can be forged, nothing is evident from within itself:

Tosafot on Gittin 22a:2:1.hebrew: עציץ של אחד וזרעים של אחר - ה"ה דהוה מצי לאשמועי' הכל בעציץ וזרעים של אחד, אלא לרבותא נקט הכי, דאע"ג דבעל עציץ קונה זרעים, לא קנה, אע"פ שהם בתוך העציץ שלו:
Tosafot on Gittin 22a:2:1.english: A pot belonging to one [person] and plants belonging to another - The same [law] could have been taught [where] both the pot and the plants belong to one [person]; rather, [the Gemara] stated it this way to [teach] a greater novelty: that even though the owner of the pot is acquiring the plants, he does not acquire [them until he takes possession], even though they are inside his pot:

Tosafot on Gittin 22a:3:1.hebrew: החזיק בזרעים קנה עציץ - צריך עיון אם צריך לומר "אגב" ו"קני" כמו בעלמא, כדאמרי' בפ"ק דקידושין (דף כז.), או שמא הכא לא צריך, דכיון דצריך עציץ לזרעים, בטל אגב זרעים. וכן גבי שטר: כיון שהחזיק בקרקע, נקנה השטר בכל מקום שהוא; ושמא התם לא בעינן "אגב", משום דשטר אפסרא דארעא הוא:
Tosafot on Gittin 22a:3:1.english: Once he took possession of the plants, he acquired the pot - It requires further study whether one must say "agav" [by way of] and "acquire" [i.e., explicitly state that the pot is acquired along with the plants], as [is required] in general, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (27a), or perhaps here it is not necessary, for since the pot is needed for the plants, it is subordinate [and acquired] by way of the plants. And similarly regarding a deed: once he has taken possession of the land, the deed is acquired wherever it may be; and perhaps there [too] we do not require [saying] "agav," because a deed is the bridle of the land [i.e., an accessory to it]:

Tosafot on Gittin 22a:5:1.hebrew: בתר נקבו אזלינן - למאן דאמר בהעור והרוטב (חולין קכח.) בדלעת הנטוע בעציץ שאינו נקוב ויצאה חוץ לעציץ, "הטמא בטומאתו והטהור בטהרתו", ה"ה אם עציץ בחוצה לארץ ונופו נוטה לארץ, דמהני יניקת הנוף לענין נוף גופיה וחייב במעשר; מכל מקום לא חשיבא יניקת הנוף כיניקת שורש, דהא לא מטהרה יניקת הנוף מה שבתוך העציץ, והכא מחייב נוף מחמת יניקת העיקר:
Tosafot on Gittin 22a:5:1.english: We follow its perforation - According to the one who says in [the chapter] Ha'or Veharotav (Chullin 128a) regarding a gourd planted in an unperforated pot that extended outside the pot, "that which is impure [remains] in its impurity, and that which is pure [remains] in its purity" — the same applies if [the] pot is outside of Eretz Yisrael and its branches extend into Eretz Yisrael, that the nourishment of the branches is effective with respect to the branches themselves, and [they are] obligated in tithes; nevertheless, the nourishment of the branches is not considered like the nourishment of a root, for the nourishment of the branches does not purify what is inside the pot, whereas here [the] branches are obligated [in tithes] on account of the nourishment of the main [root]:

Tosafot on Gittin 22a:7:1.hebrew: ובדאשרוש לא פליגי והתנן שתי גנות כו' - קס"ד דהא דקתני סיפא: "א"ר מאיר: ומה אם ירצה העליון כו'", שאין זה עיקר הטעם, מדקתני נמי התם: "א"ר מאיר: מאחר ששניהן יכולין למחות זה על זה, רואין מהיכן ירק זה חי", משמע דבסברא פליגי אי זה מהן עיקר. ואמרי' נמי התם בגמרא בפ' הבית והעלייה (ב"מ דף קיח:): "ואזדו לטעמייהו, אילן היוצא מן הגזע כו'". ותנן נמי גבי ערלה כי האי גוונא, ותימה דלא מייתי הכא מערלה:
Tosafot on Gittin 22a:7:1.english: And do they not disagree with regard to [a case] where it took root? But didn't we learn [in a Mishnah]: two gardens, etc. - [The Gemara] initially assumed regarding that which the latter clause [of that Mishnah] teaches — "Rabbi Meir said: What if the upper [owner] wishes, etc." — that this is not the primary reason, since it also teaches there: "Rabbi Meir said: Since both of them can protest against one another, we look at from where this vegetable draws its sustenance," which implies that they disagree in reasoning as to which of them is primary. And we also say there in the Gemara in the chapter [entitled] HaBayit veHaAliyah (Bava Metzia 118b): "And they follow their own reasoning, [as in the case of] a tree that grows out of the trunk, etc." And we also learned [in a Mishnah] regarding orlah in a similar manner, and it is astonishing that [the Gemara] does not cite [a proof] here from orlah:
